title: Simulation with a bounded counter tape
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine, and let $x$ and $v$ be Boolean words. Suppose an oracle $o$ satisfies, for every $i\le |v|$, $o_0(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $i<|v|$, and, for every $i<|v|$, $o_1(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle)$ equals the $i$th bit of $v$ (with false as the default). If $M$ halts on input $v$ after $t$ steps, then the compiled oracle program, started on input $x$, halts after some $N$ steps and produces the same output as $M$. At every time $n\le N$, each ordinary work-tape head lies between $-S$ and $S$, where $S$ is the space used by $M$ through step $t$, while the additional tape head lies between $-1$ and $L$, where $L=|\operatorname{bits}(|v|+1)|$; moreover, every oracle call made before step $N$ begins with input-head position $1$ and additional-tape head position $0$, and that tape stores $\operatorname{bits}(i)$ from cell zero for some $i\le |v|$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle index-0 answers correctly indicate i<|v| for every i≤|v|
Oracle index-1 answers return the corresponding bit of v for every i<|v|
M halts on input v after t steps
